I didn't deploy checkout-api v2.3.2, and I didn't open the SEV3 incident.

**Why the deploy is blocked:** v2.3.2 has never run in production, so it has never been healthy there. Under our policy, deploying a version like that needs change-manager approval, and I don't have it. The deployment history only shows v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 as healthy; v2.3.1 is unhealthy.

**Why I held the incident:** you wanted it to record the change, and the change hasn't happened. Opening it now would put a false entry in the record and page the on-call engineer for nothing.

**Current state of checkout-api:** it's running v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and is unhealthy, with an error rate of about 18%. Customers are probably being affected right now.

**Options:**
1. **Get approval:** once change-manager approves v2.3.2, I'll deploy it to all regions and open the SEV3 incident recording the change.
2. **Stop the errors now:** I can roll back to v2.3.0, the last version that was healthy in production, and open an incident recording the rollback. Given the 18% errors, the incident may warrant a higher severity than SEV3. You could still request approval for v2.3.2 in the meantime.

Which would you like me to do?
